The interview is a retrospective self-report and may contain post-hoc reframing.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I was the Product Manager for onboarding at CollabHub... My responsibility was to identify a credible response quickly without derailing the sprint roadmap or putting enterprise customers at greater risk.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant states the operational objective and constraints without a manifested hidden bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: At first, the dashboard only showed account setup as one broad stage... I asked our data analyst to investigate the funnel instrumentation and asked a designer to pull heatmap analytics.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The investigation actions are a reasonable response to an underspecified dashboard signal.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: In the immediate sense, reduce abandonment and protect activation rate... We had to decide whether this was a narrow usability or payment issue, or evidence that our whole onboarding approach was behind where the market was going.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This frames competing product objectives and hypotheses but does not manifest the hidden instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I chose a rapid internal analytics review, supplemented by a light competitor scan, rather than immediately commissioning user interviews.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is decision point 1; the hidden manifest assigns no bias there.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I had the 32% increase in the broad account-setup drop-off step, no fresh qualitative feedback, and a warning from the analyst that the payment sub-step had incomplete instrumentation... We had only five weeks until the board review.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: These are the evidence and timing constraints available before decision point 1.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We needed a directional answer within days, not weeks... I documented that we were choosing speed over depth and asked Research to hold provisional time in case the data stayed unclear.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly documents a speed-versus-depth tradeoff and preserves a fallback research option.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The analyst narrowed the issue. Abandonment rose most clearly after payment details... So it was suggestive, but not statistically stable.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant appropriately characterizes a small, incompletely instrumented cohort signal as suggestive but unstable.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once I was preparing options for the VP of Product. The competitor review showed three named platforms had shipped guided setup experiences... An industry newsletter was describing guided setup as something most leading SaaS onboarding flows were adopting.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This records external context that became relevant; the hidden occurrence is mapped to the subsequent weighting-and-choice rationale.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Whether to build an AI-guided setup wizard, focus on the payment-detail issue, or run a small A/B test of both directions before committing.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This states the alternatives at decision point 2 without yet expressing the hidden mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Internally, we had the payment-field signal, but it was from a small cohort... Externally, we had a much more visible pattern: competitors were changing their onboarding experiences...
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant inventories competing evidence sources before explaining how they were weighted.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I put more weight on the external pattern than I normally would have... I decided the AI-guided wizard was the better strategic move, and we would address the payment field within that broader redesign later.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is the sole hidden instance: adoption prevalence among competitors and peer PMs is used as the primary basis for choosing the wizard while the internal payment signal is downweighted.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I ruled it out because it would have taken design and engineering time without giving us a board-ready feature direction quickly. Also, I felt that waiting while the market moved would make us look late.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The manifest contains no additional occurrence at the A/B-test decision; the stated deadline and communication rationale remain a plausible non-bias explanation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I probably would have pushed harder for the payment-field experiment first. The external activity was a major reason I was comfortable making a larger commitment despite the uncertainty in our own data.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is corroborating counterfactual evidence for the mapped instance, not a separate hidden occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I had to decide whether to fully reassign two engineers from the enterprise bug-fix backlog for three sprints, split their time... or delay the wizard and prioritize the backlog.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is decision point 3, which the hidden specification identifies as non-biased.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I authorized the full reallocation to the wizard... I accepted the bug-risk trade-off, with the engineering lead agreeing to triage only production-severity issues during the build.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The staffing decision is explained through capacity, feature completeness, board visibility, and an explicit risk mitigation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Two enterprise tickets escalated during that period... The wizard build stayed on schedule. At the same time, a follow-up analytics review continued to show payment-field friction.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This reports consequences and persistent evidence without adding a hidden bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Whether to release the wizard to all new signups before the board review, limit it to a 10% canary release, or wait another week for more regression testing and improved payment instrumentation... The board meeting was four days away.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is decision point 4 framing under technical and board-review constraints.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: A 10% canary would have been safer technically, but it would not produce enough usable operational evidence before the board meeting. Waiting another week would have improved testing, but it would also leave us presenting a plan rather than a shipped response.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The hidden specification assigns no bias to decision point 4; the candidate escalation interpretation is not affirmatively supported.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The post-launch activation rate did not show a statistically significant change from the prior month... We then prioritized a focused review of payment validation and instrumentation.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant assesses the launch outcome and redirects work toward the unresolved payment issue.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I would have run the controlled comparison and recruited several users from the new account cohort. I would also have kept the wizard in a limited canary longer.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a retrospective improvement plan and not a new manifested occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: A larger, stable cohort showing that payment details were clearly the dominant exit point would have changed it... If that evidence had been strong, I would have treated the payment fix as the immediate priority.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant identifies evidence that would have changed the redesign decision.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: If the competitors had not introduced guided onboarding at that time... I think I would have been more willing to make the smaller, targeted payment change first.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a counterfactual explanation of the earlier choice, not a second hidden instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: selecting the onboarding redesign approach
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The PM selects the redesign mainly because competitors and peer PMs rapidly adopted the same pattern, treating adoption prevalence as the primary evidentiary signal while downweighting internal cohort evidence pointing to payment-field friction.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Bandwagon effect is an established equivalent label for Herding in this context; the finding identifies adoption by many peers as the reason for adopting the same course.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures the defining external-adoption prevalence signal, the contrast with internal payment-field evidence, and the affected redesign-choice operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The three quoted excerpts are valid participant statements and directly support the identified weighting and choice. The wording uses 'he' once, but the attributed speaker and evidence are otherwise correct.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The candidate concerns continuing a previously chosen wizard under launch pressure and does not capture the hidden Herding mechanism of using peer and competitor adoption prevalence to weight evidence. Its valid quote localizes to negative segment seg_018.

The candidate is localized to the same episode but proposes a distinct salience/availability mechanism rather than the full Herding mechanism. It also duplicates the already matched obs_001 claim and cannot create an additional true positive.

candidates.details: The launch-rationale quote is valid but supports a time-bounded communication and risk-management trade-off. It localizes to a negative segment and does not match the hidden Herding mechanism.

The candidate uses valid evidence from the positive segment, but availability is a distinct, less complete explanation of the same social-evidence episode. Because obs_001 already matches herd_01, this candidate is a duplicate at the fourth threshold.

high_only.detection_interpretation: The sole hidden segment is missed because the only identified occurrence is moderate confidence.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The moderate-confidence identified occurrence localizes to the sole positive segment.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All identified findings produce the same segment-level result because the only identified finding is moderate confidence.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Candidate inclusion preserves the hit but adds one false alarm on negative seg_018; the other candidate duplicates the positive-segment claim.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: The candidate describes persistence after commitment and board-facing progress concerns, not adoption-prevalence-driven evidence weighting.
The candidate shares the same recent peer and competitor evidence but frames it as salience, not as adopting a course because others adopted it; it duplicates the already matched claim.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly reports that retrieved corpus support was not used and supplies no corpus evidence. No citation metadata was provided, so corpus fidelity is unavailable but there is no citation inconsistency to score.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: The identified Herding-equivalent finding enters at moderate confidence: segment hits increase from 0 to 1 and strict/mechanism-first instance F1 increases from 0.0 to 1.0.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No change; there are no low-confidence identified findings.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Candidate inclusion leaves recall unchanged but adds one segment false alarm and two instance false positives; segment F1 falls to 0.6667 and instance F1 falls to 0.5.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the run detects the sole positive segment with no segment false alarms: 1 hit, 0 misses, 0 false alarms, and 21 correct rejections.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At the recommended threshold, the run achieves 1 true positive, 0 false negatives, and 0 false positives; the bandwagon effect label is an approved equivalent of Herding.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first scoring is identical to strict scoring at every threshold because the identified label is an approved equivalent and neither candidate supplies an additional full-mechanism match.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: Candidates are useful diagnostically but add noise at the fourth threshold: one plausible but unsupported negative-segment candidate and one duplicate near-miss on the already detected instance.
main_failure_modes: The only true occurrence is moderate rather than high confidence, so high_only scoring misses it.
Candidate inclusion adds a false alarm and a duplicate prediction.
The availability candidate is not separable as a full mechanism from the identified bandwagon/Herding occurrence.
main_strengths: The identified occurrence is correctly localized to the decision-point-2 evidence-weighting segment.
The bandwagon effect label and mechanism are an approved equivalent/full match for the hidden Herding instance.
The identified evidence quotes are valid and support the decision effect.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This is a strong identified-finding run at the recommended threshold, with perfect primary segment and instance results before candidate inclusion. The result also illustrates the cost of adding candidate detections: candidate-tier recall does not improve, while false alarms and duplicate predictions increase.
